body: I think I may have made my earlier descriptions confusing. The "alternate convention" is that the products of intertia themselves are computed as positive products (eg. $I_{xy} = \Sigma m_i x_i y_i$) and then negated when placed in the tensor; it has nothing to do with the order in which they're presented. The choice of order $(I_{yz}, I_{xz}, I_{xy})$ comes from Voigt notation (or specifically the second half of a tensor in Voigt notation). It's the least arbitrary order to chose, in my opinion.
Yes, not sure how that happened. I'll fix it.
That's a good idea. Noted.

I was copying the implementation from the `set_mass`, `set_inertia`, and `set_center_of_mass` functions. Looking at them again, I realize now that those if statements are actually there to avoid having to call `_update_mass_properties` if not necessary. The `set_mass_properties` function calls it regardless, so I agree; I'll get rid of the if statements for mass, inertia, and product_of_inertia.

body:
The XY, XZ, YZ order comes from the typical order used in Geometric Algebra, which is to specify each pair of dimensions in a dimensionally-increasing order. The YZ, XZ, XY order comes from symmetry with 3D rotations in most game engines, where we think of things as rotating "around" X, but it's actually in the YZ plane. So we fill the Vector's X, Y, and Z components with the YZ, XZ, and XY rotations, respectively.

IMO, it is more intuitive to be consistent with the 3D rotation order used in the rest of the engine, even if these are not rotations. Users of 3D can intuitively understand the concept of the X value containing the value that exists perpendicular to the X axis, even if technically that acts on everything but X. For my 4D module I often chose to put things in YZ, XZ, XY, XW, YW, ZW order in the exposed API, to build on the intuitions of 3D users.

TL;DR: I think the version in this PR is good.

body: The documentation for this property should either explain or link to sources that explain how to convert between this representation (inertia diagonal and product of inertia) and the other representations, like inertia principle axes plus Quaternion, and inertia tensor. Alternatively, we could have other properties for the other representations, but considering we have `set_mass_properties` as the recommended way to set everything at once, maybe it's better to just document this and leave that task to callers... but the callers still need to know what to do.
